title: Parallel Tool Calls and Streaming with Tools

questions.question: An assistant looks up three independent records one after another, and the total wait is the sum of all three lookups. What is the fix?
options: Ask the user to request only one record at a time
Make each lookup slower so the timing evens out
Cache the user's question and skip the lookups
Run the independent lookups concurrently and match each result to its request
questions.explanation: Independent waits overlap instead of adding up. This lesson builds the parallel fan-out, plus the id matching that keeps results lined up.

questions.question: How does StreamAccumulator keep interleaved argument chunks separate?
options: It appends every chunk to one global string
It appends each chunk to the buffer named by its call id
It sorts chunks alphabetically before decoding them
It executes a call as soon as its first chunk arrives
questions.explanation: Each call_start creates a CallBuffer keyed by id, and later args_delta events append only to that buffer.

questions.question: What does CallBuffer.try_parse return before call_stop marks the buffer done?
options: An empty Call with default city
A partially parsed dictionary
None
A decode error for every partial chunk
questions.explanation: try_parse waits for done so incomplete JSON is not decoded; once done it calls json.loads on the complete argument string.

questions.question: Which complete argument object is reconstructed for the fake stream's C call?
options: {city: Bengaluru}
{city: Tokyo}
{city: Zurich, units: celsius}
{"city":"Zurich"}
questions.explanation: The C chunks are {"city":"Zu, rich"}, yielding the valid JSON object with city Zurich and no units field.

questions.question: Why does replay_and_execute return a result mapping rather than a list in arrival order?
options: Results are keyed by call id
Lists cannot hold JSON values
The code uses city names as globally unique thread ids
The executor returns no result until all calls have identical latency
questions.explanation: The stream may interleave calls and futures may finish out of order; call ids preserve the request-to-result association.

questions.question: When should an application avoid parallelizing otherwise independent tool calls?
options: When all calls return strings
When order-dependent side effects or shared state are involved
When a call has a JSON object argument
When the tool registry contains more than one function
questions.explanation: Parallel execution is safe only when operations are independent; writes or order-sensitive effects may require sequential coordination.
